reconstruction_additions.purpose: EP04 camera-only hand MOTION reconstruction explanation; supporting original-paper figure crops, not scientific results generated by DoF.
reconstruction_additions.method: Original PDF pages rendered/cropped with Poppler at 300 dpi; no AI image redraw.

figures.credit: Romero, Tzionas & Black · MANO / Embodied Hands · SIGGRAPH Asia 2017 · Fig. 6
figures.context: Top: scans of one subject in different poses. Bottom: corresponding mesh alignments. Useful for observed geometry versus a shared articulated surface representation.
figures.showing_sequence: These are selected captured poses, not certified consecutive temporal frames. Do not label this strip t0/t1/t2 as a time sequence.
figures.animation_suggestion: Reveal observed scan first, then corresponding fitted mesh below. Zoom two or three pose pairs rather than displaying all tiny hands. Explain that a stable model preserves vertex correspondence; the figure itself is a pose collection.
caveats: The top row is textured scans, not a visualization of raw unstructured points. Do not call those images raw point clouds.
The fitted pink surface is a registration result; fitting does not prove real-time tracking or perfect unseen geometry.

detail_crop.description: First three selected pose pairs, scan above fitted mesh. Not consecutive time frames.

figures.credit: Romero, Tzionas & Black · MANO / Embodied Hands · SIGGRAPH Asia 2017 · Fig. 9
figures.context: Two hand poses illustrating pose-dependent shape corrections. Columns left to right: model without corrections (red); with corrections (green); registration (pink); red/pink overlay; green/pink overlay; personalized template (cyan); template plus pose corrections (yellow). Corrections are applied to the template before articulation.
figures.animation_suggestion: Start with cyan personalized template; reveal yellow pose correction; show red versus green articulated result and pink scan registration. Animate cropping/highlights without claiming interpolation itself is a measured trajectory.
caveats: This figure visualizes pose-corrective blend shapes and articulation, not a monocular estimator or a capture-accuracy benchmark.
Shape identity beta and pose theta are different. Beta is typically held fixed for an individual sequence while theta and global transform change per frame.
MANO is a 2017 method despite this arXiv copy having a 2022 identifier.

figures.credit: Wang et al. · HO-Cap · Fig. 4 · arXiv:2406.06843
figures.context: Multiview RGB-D frames feed hand and object estimation. The hand branch uses MediaPipe 2D joints, filtering, triangulation/RANSAC, hand pose optimization, then joint hand-object refinement. MANO shape is calibrated per subject and hand pose is fitted across observations.
figures.animation_suggestion: Pan from synchronized RGB/depth views to the right-hand joint estimation branch, then joint refinement and the final fitted geometry. Label as dataset reconstruction/annotation pipeline.
caveats: The full HO-Cap setup also includes a worn HoloLens; visibly present in the original figure. This is not the recommended fully non-worn capture setup.
Temporal interpolation and smoothing use offline sequence context; do not present the diagram as a causal real-time controller.
Their initial SDF-only hand fitting was insufficient. 2D/3D joints anchor the fit; it is not arbitrary triangulation of point-cloud neighbors.

existing_assets_inspected.credit: Handa et al. · DexPilot · Fig. 4 · arXiv:1910.03135
existing_assets_inspected.fit: Most direct example of multi-camera point cloud -> learned pose priors + articulated real-time tracking -> kinematic retargeting -> robot control. DART articulated model should not be mislabeled as MANO.
Direct monocular RGB -> ViT/transformer -> pose, shape, camera -> MANO mesh; no point cloud intermediate required. The white hand overlay is an estimated mesh, not a glove.

existing_assets_inspected.credit: Pavlakos et al. · HaMeR · official project demo
existing_assets_inspected.fit: Actual framewise hand mesh results in motion. Useful to show time varying mesh, but neither video smoothness nor aligned benchmark error proves absolute teleoperation accuracy.

technical_bridge: Observation is not representation: camera RGB/depth data are evidence; point clouds represent sampled observed surface, joints represent articulated state, and a fitted mesh represents a continuous model surface.
For depth frame z(u,v), back-project through camera intrinsics; for multiple cameras, transform samples with calibrated camera extrinsics into a common frame. Occluded surfaces remain unobserved.
A consistent hand surface is usually a structured articulated template fitted or regressed to observations, not a generic connection of nearby points.

Conceptually, M_t = W(T_bar + B_S(beta) + B_P(theta_t), J(beta), theta_t, skinning_weights), followed by the global transform. This is an explanatory MANO/SMPL-style formulation, not a newly measured model.

Hold identity shape beta fixed within a person; estimate pose theta_t and global hand transform over time. Temporal regularization limits jitter but excessive smoothing introduces lag. Maintain occlusion confidence rather than pretending hidden fingers were observed.
Reconstruction accuracy, temporal stability, absolute robot-frame registration, and end-to-end teleoperation task success are distinct evaluation axes.
